description: Lunar Archives is a team of curious, creative, and technology-driven minds working together to uncover the stories behind NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. We bring together coding, data analysis, research, visualization, animation, and storytelling to transform forgotten pieces of space exploration into meaningful discoveries. We welcome passionate collaborators who are eager to learn, share ideas, and build something impactful together.
summary: Lunar Archives is an interactive digital archive documenting human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through a unified collection, visitors can explore these objects, discover their original missions, understand their scientific contributions and learn about their present-day status. The website brings together research, historical context, visual references and individual object profiles, with filters to explore lunar and Martian missions. Designed to make space exploration accessible to school-age enthusiasts and the wider public, Lunar Archives transforms scattered mission information into an engaging digital museum that preserves the stories of humanity's exploration beyond Earth.
details:
Lunar Archives is an interactive digital museum preserving the stories of human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars. Landers, rovers and mission equipment represent chapters in humanity’s exploration of space, yet information about them is scattered across mission reports, archives, images and technical documents. Lunar Archives brings these stories together in an accessible experience.

Visitors can choose the Moon or Mars, browse the collection and explore object records to learn about each object’s mission, purpose, history and status. The archive currently lists 31 objects, with status information and some details and images still being added.

The website combines research and storytelling with interactive features. Its experience includes 3D models that visitors can rotate and zoom, numbered points that explain model components, sound controls and voice narration. The design is hosted on Netlify and makes the collection accessible through a browser, while its object structure allows the archive to grow as information is added.

Created by an international team contributing across project leadership, research, engineering, CAD and visual design, and front-end development, Lunar Archives aims to make space exploration history easier to discover and understand. Its purpose is to preserve humanity’s footprints beyond Earth and inspire curiosity about exploration.

We built the site with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with JSON for the data. There are no frameworks. The fonts are Instrument Serif, Manrope and IBM Plex Mono from Google Fonts. We worked in Visual Studio Code, kept the project on GitHub and host it on Netlify. We used ChatGPT and Claude for coding help.
